subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` deliberately fail closed for shipped legacy session rows whose `pluginOwnerId` is absent?
rationale: Exact-owner authorization is the safer security boundary, but v2026.6.11 contains the ownership surface and upgraded installations can retain older ownerless rows, so accepting the new operator-visible failure mode requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed for ownerless rows
options.body: Require an exact persisted owner match and document or prove that operators and non-plugin clients remain the recovery path.

options.title: Add a trusted migration
options.body: Define an operator- or doctor-owned migration that assigns verified ownership before plugin-runtime patch access is permitted.

recommendation.title: Fail closed for ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Require an exact persisted owner match and document or prove that operators and non-plugin clients remain the recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the most recent direct history on the sibling session lifecycle handler and is the strongest available owner for the authorization-versus-upgrade decision.
